recipes.description: The original cocktail: whiskey, sugar, bitters, water.
recipes.notes: Stir with ice about 20 seconds — you want dilution and chill without clouding. Express the orange twist over the drink before dropping it in.
steps: Add simple syrup (or sugar cube + water) and bitters to a rocks glass.
Add bourbon and a large ice cube.
Stir 20 seconds until chilled and diluted.
Express an orange twist over the glass and drop it in.
recipes.title: Old Fashioned

recipes.description: Rye, sweet vermouth, and bitters — the Manhattan's drier, spicier soul.
recipes.notes: Use a decent sweet vermouth and keep it refrigerated once opened. Rye is traditional; bourbon makes a sweeter Manhattan.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 20–30 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a cherry.
recipes.title: Manhattan

recipes.description: Whiskey's answer to the Negroni: bourbon, Campari, sweet vermouth.
recipes.notes: Equal-parts (1 oz each) also works and is closer to the original 1927 spec — try both and pick your ratio.
steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir 20 seconds until chilled.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Express an orange twist over the glass and drop it in.
recipes.title: Boulevardier

recipes.description: Bright and frothy — lemon and bourbon with a silky cap.
recipes.notes: Skip the egg white if you prefer; the drink is still excellent. Dry-shake (no ice) first if using egg white, then shake with ice.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker (no ice if using egg white) and shake 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass, or into a coupe without ice.
recipes.title: Whiskey Sour

recipes.description: Crisp, cold, and brutally simple. The king of cocktails.
recipes.notes: Stir, don't shake — shaking clouds it and over-dilutes. Keep gin and glassware cold; vermouth goes in the fridge after opening.
steps: Chill a coupe or martini glass.
Add gin and vermouth to a mixing glass with plenty of ice.
Stir 20–30 seconds until ice-cold.
Strain into the chilled glass.
Express a lemon twist over the drink, or drop in an olive.
recipes.title: Dry Martini

recipes.description: Equal parts gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth. Bitter, bold, perfect.
recipes.notes: Built in the glass works fine — no mixing glass required. A Negroni Sbagliato swaps the gin for prosecco.
steps: Add all ingredients to a rocks glass with a large ice cube.
Stir briefly to chill and combine.
Express an orange twist over the glass and drop it in.
recipes.title: Negroni

recipes.description: Gin, tonic, ice, citrus — simplicity done right.
recipes.notes: Use plenty of ice and cold tonic — a warm, flat G&T is a sad thing. Fever-Tree or Q are reliable tonics.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add gin.
Top with chilled tonic and stir once gently.
Garnish with a lime wedge.
recipes.title: Gin & Tonic

recipes.description: Rum, lime, sugar. Nothing to hide behind — balance is everything.
recipes.notes: The test of a good rum and fresh limes. Adjust syrup a touch to taste — limes vary.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
recipes.title: Daiquiri

recipes.description: Mint, lime, rum, and fizz — the Cuban cooler.
recipes.notes: Muddle mint gently — press, don't shred, or it turns bitter. Slap the garnish mint between your palms to release aroma.
steps: Gently muddle mint with lime juice and syrup in a highball glass.
Add rum and fill with crushed ice.
Top with club soda and stir briefly.
Garnish with a mint sprig.
recipes.title: Mojito

recipes.description: The tiki classic: aged rum, lime, curaçao, and orgeat.

ingredients.item: Aged rum (Jamaican-style if you have it)

recipes.notes: 1944 Trader Vic's spec. Orgeat is the soul of the drink — don't skip it.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake 10 seconds.
Strain over crushed ice in a rocks glass.
Garnish with mint and the spent lime shell.
recipes.title: Mai Tai

recipes.description: Tequila, lime, orange liqueur, salt. Sunshine in a glass.
recipes.notes: Fresh lime juice only — never sour mix. Salt half the rim so drinkers can choose.
steps: Salt the rim of a rocks glass if desired; fill with ice.
Add tequila, lime juice, and orange liqueur to a shaker with ice.
Shake 10–12 seconds.
Strain into the glass and garnish with a lime wheel.
recipes.title: Margarita

recipes.description: Tequila and grapefruit soda — Mexico's actual favorite highball.
recipes.notes: A pinch of salt in the drink itself (not just the rim) sharpens everything.
steps: Salt the rim of a highball glass if desired; fill with ice.
Add tequila and lime juice.
Top with grapefruit soda and stir gently.
Garnish with a grapefruit wedge.
recipes.title: Paloma

recipes.description: Vodka, cranberry, lime, orange — the '90s icon, done properly.
recipes.notes: It should be pale pink, not red — go easy on the cranberry.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard 10–12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express a lime twist over the drink.
recipes.title: Cosmopolitan

recipes.description: Vodka, espresso, coffee liqueur — dessert and a nightcap in one.
recipes.notes: Shake hard — the foam cap is the whole point. Fresh espresso matters; cold brew works in a pinch.
steps: Add all ingredients to a shaker with plenty of ice.
Shake hard 12–15 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Float 3 coffee beans on the foam.
recipes.title: Espresso Martini

recipes.description: Vodka, lime, and spicy ginger beer in a copper mug.
recipes.notes: Ginger beer, not ginger ale — you want the bite. The copper mug is tradition, not requirement.
steps: Fill a copper mug or highball with ice.
Add vodka and lime juice.
Top with ginger beer and stir gently.
Garnish with a lime wheel.
recipes.title: Moscow Mule

recipes.description: Bitter orange, prosecco, and soda — Italy's golden hour.
recipes.notes: 3-2-1: prosecco, Aperol, soda. Build over ice in the glass — no shaker needed.
steps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Add prosecco, then Aperol, then soda.
Stir once gently and garnish with an orange slice.
recipes.title: Aperol Spritz
